quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: What is the best group formation when riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway?
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation on straight roads. Switch to single-file when going through curves, making turns, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while riding?

options.text: Keep going and hope to wake up.
Get off the road and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: You can see through the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when the pavement is slippery, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy. Wet roads require more stopping distance.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to maintain your balance.
Maintain your speed to improve traction.
Not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and proceed as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and proceed as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery roads when possible. If you must cross one, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as you can.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear brightly colored clothes, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals to help others see you.

questions.question: How can you see better when riding at night?

options.text: Using the headlights of the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the headlights of the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Use the headlights of the vehicle ahead to see the road better. Increase your following distance and slow down when riding in the dark.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, all of the following matter, except:

options.text: The helmet does not have any defects.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly and have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: Guarantees that they will yield to you.
Doesn't mean that they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doesn't mean that they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look at motorcyclists but still fail to actually see them.

questions.question: How do many over-the-counter drugs affect riding?

options.text: Only affect your riding if you drink along with taking the medication.
Have the same effect on everyone.

questions.explanation: Like alcohol, many drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal) have side effects that can harm your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Not worry about them and just focus on the road in front of you.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let tailgaters pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster and more dangerously. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers do not expect vehicles there.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo, what happens to your motorcycle's performance?

options.text: It speeds up faster but takes longer to stop.
It takes longer to speed up and longer to stop.
It takes longer to speed up but stops faster.
It speeds up faster and stops faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes longer to speed up and longer to stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo slows down your motorcycle. It takes longer to accelerate and longer to stop.

questions.question: What does eye contact with other drivers really mean?

options.text: It is not worth your effort.
It does not guarantee they will give you the right of way.
It guarantees they will give you the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will give you the right of way.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look at motorcyclists but do not actually see them.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The rear brake is operated with your right foot.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. This signal tells other riders to follow you.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until it loses interest.
Slow down as you approach it, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach it, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: What should you do if you are riding alongside another vehicle?

options.text: Stay alongside until the next exit.
Let the other driver handle it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in their blind spot, and they could block your escape route if a hazard appears. Speed up or drop back to get out of this position.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: A front brake and a rear brake.
A front brake, a rear brake, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: A front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: When a group of riders merges onto a highway, what formation should they use?
questions.explanation: Use single file when merging onto a highway, turning, or taking curves. Staggered formation is better for normal riding conditions.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, how should you do it?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Perform braking and swerving separately. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: If you carry a load in a sidecar, how does it affect your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Extra weight increases your motorcycle's mass and inertia. This makes stopping distance longer. Start slowing down and stopping earlier when carrying a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: Many factors affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Which one does NOT affect BAC?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway from a ramp on your right may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of your lane so they can share it, if needed.
Move into another lane, if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if needed.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles merging onto the highway. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them room to enter safely.

questions.question: What is the normal following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle in front of you. Increase this distance in bad weather or poor conditions.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up
Only when there is heavy traffic
Any time you plan to change lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan to change lanes
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: The front tire powers the bike, so you lose acceleration
The flat tire shakes the bike, making mirrors hard to use

questions.explanation: A flat front tire is very dangerous because it affects your steering ability. If your front tire goes flat while riding, exit the road safely as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Learn where all your motorcycle controls are located before you ride. The horn button is usually next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes involve:

options.text: Riders with little experience on their motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with little experience on their motorcycle
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders who are new to their motorcycle.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids from braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake
Release both brakes and coast to a stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks from braking, release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates are all more dangerous than dry pavement.
